alerts.title: Permanent fire prohibition on Teewah Beach
alerts.description: A QPWS imposed fire prohibition is in place in the Cooloola Recreation Area, except at Poverty Point camping area. Camp fires must not be lit anywhere else in the recreation area including in the Teewah Beach camping zones 1-7.
alerts.details:
A QPWS imposed fire prohibition is in place in the Cooloola Recreation Area, except at Poverty Point camping area. Camp fires must not be lit anywhere else in the recreation area including in the Teewah Beach camping zones 1-7.

This permanent fire prohibition was implemented to reduce the risk of bushfires, protect critical habitat of native wildlife, enhance visitor safety from camp fire related injuries and reduce rubbish from non-combustible materials being burnt.

Fully enclosed cooking and heating appliances can still be used in camping areas that meet the below requirements.

  • The appliance must use gas or manufactured fuel (heat beads, briquettes). Manufactured fuel does not include timber or wood.
  • It must be used only for cooking and/or heating.
  • It must be a minimum of 20cm off the ground and more than 2m from flammable materials, which includes vegetation. 
  • It must not have the potential to generate airborne embers, or possibly ignite nearby ground fuels.
  • It must be fully self-contained (heat source enclosed and no exposed flame) and never left unattended when in use.
  • Appliances that are not fully self-contained, such as braziers, are not permitted.
  • All appliances, materials and burnt fuel must be removed from the recreation area on your departure.

On-the-spot fines of $863 can be issued to people who light fires during a fire prohibition.

Camp fires are permitted at Poverty Point camping area and at nearby Inskip Peninsula Recreation Area unless as fire ban or prohibition is in place. Always check local directions and signs before lighting a fire. 

For details on the difference between a Queensland Fire Department (QFD) total fire ban and a QPWS fire prohibition and approved cooking appliances visit the DETSI Camp fires and cooking web page.

 

Please monitor park alerts on the department's website for updated information.

alerts.description: George Point camping area on the southern coastline of Hinchinbrook Island National Park has been affected by severe erosion due to ongoing high tides over the past several years.
alerts.details:
George Point camping area on the southern coastline of Hinchinbrook Island National Park has been affected by severe erosion due to ongoing high tides over the past several years.

The camping area signage and infrastructure, including the toilet, have been removed. There is currently no signage to identify the pickup point for hikers.

There is bush camping available nearby if needed by Thorsborne Trail hikers or sea kayakers. Space for camping is available under a large stand of trees approximately 2.6km south of the Mulligan Creek crossing along the beach (prior to reaching the old camping area when hiking from north to south). Look out for a sign identifying the new camping area. Please be aware there is no toilet/pack rack. There is no boat-based camping available.

The George Point pickup point is 250m southwest of the bush camping space, along the beach.

QPWS is currently reviewing options for the future of the site as part of the Thorsborne Trail Enhancement project.

alerts.title: Inskip Peninsula camping area boundary realignment and access changes following severe weather damage, combined with shoreline retrogression
alerts.description: A combination of ex-Tropical Cyclone Alfred damage, storm surges, swell, and shoreline retrogression has eroded the eastern-facing beaches of Inskip Peninsula, and caused loss of sand, destabilisation of the dunes and loss of existing campground border fencing.
alerts.details:
A combination of ex-Tropical Cyclone Alfred damage, storm surges, swell, and shoreline retrogression has eroded the eastern-facing beaches of Inskip Peninsula, and caused loss of sand, destabilisation of the dunes and loss of existing campground border fencing.

A team of geotechnical erosion experts was engaged to investigate the impacts of cyclone events at the Inskip Peninsula Recreation Area and to provide technical advice regarding site safety. Based on the findings and recommendations from the geotechnical assessment, the camping area boundaries will be realigned to establish a 20-metre retrogression buffer zone landward of the current treeline.

This boundary realignment is necessary due to ongoing coastal erosion, nearshore landslide risk, and damage sustained to existing infrastructure. The revised layout will enhance visitor safety by reducing exposure to unstable shoreline areas and future erosion hazards. The following changes apply:

M.V. SARAWAK:

  • Beachfront campsites and the former access track are no longer accessible, including the area known as “Millionaire’s Row”. This location, previously favoured by campers for its open access to solar, firmer surface, and beach proximity, is now closed.
  • Caravans are not suitable in the M.V. Sarawak camping area due to narrow access tracks and stands of cypress and oak trees.
  • When entering M.V. Sarawak, follow all signage and take the first left access track.
  • Do not proceed straight ahead—this route is now a dead end.

M.V. BEAGLE:

  • Beachfront campsites and the former beachfront access track are no longer accessible.
  • Caravans are not suitable in the M.V. Beagle camping area due to narrow access tracks and soft sand.
  • When entering M.V. Beagle, follow the signage and take the first left access track.
  • Do not proceed straight ahead—this route is now a dead end.

M.V. NATONE:

  • The Natone entrance track and eastern low lying camping areas are no longger accessible. Entry and exit to Natone is now through the former exit.
  • Caravans are not suitable in the M.V. Natone camping area due to narrow access tracks, soft sand and inability to turn around.
  • Camping in Natone is suitable to smaller tents and high clearance 4WD only. 

SS Dorrigo and Sarawak West remain the only Inskip camping areas suitable for caravans, requiring a high-clearance caravan towed by a high-clearance 4WD.

Observe all signage, barriers and directions from rangers, and do not enter closed areas.

Apply for a camping permit refund online at www.qld.gov.au/camping. Log into your account and cancel your booking to receive an automatic refund or request to change your booking to another camping area at Inskip. 

QPWS thanks you for your support and cooperation.

alerts.title: Natural Sand Movement and access to Double Island Point
alerts.description: Deep hole formations which may restrict access to and from Double Island Point
alerts.details:
Deep hole formations which may restrict access to and from Double Island Point

Regular sand movement within the saltwater lagoon at Double Island Point often results in the formation of deep holes. These natural changes can prevent vehicles from accessing the Double Island Point (Wide Bay side), the sandspit or travelling through to Rainbow Beach at any tide. This is a natural process within the Great Sandy National Park, where all environments are protected and natural coastal processes are allowed to occur.

Queensland Parks and Wildife Service maintains safe access to the beaches via the Freshwater Track and the Leisha Track.

Always drive the beaches within the Great Sandy National Park to the prevailing conditions.

As a result of the erosion, the entrance and exit tracks have merged into a single narrow lane, requiring vehicles travelling in both directions to share the same track. These conditions are most constrained during high tide periods, when available beach width is minimal.


Visitors are strongly advised to plan travel two hours either side of low tide only, proceed with caution through the single-track section, and allow additional time for delays.


Barge operations and recommended travel times may change in response to tides and weather conditions. Visitors travelling to K’gari via the Inskip barge landing must remain up to date with Mantaray Barge advice prior to departure.


Coastal conditions are dynamic and may change rapidly. Remember:

• Check tide times – only travel 2 hours either side of low tide to K’gari.

• Only access the Inskip spit barge area when safe to do so.

• Keep barge access area clear (fishing or swimming or parking vehicles near barge access is prohibited – you will be moved on if impeding traffic. Camp in fenced areas when possible.)

alerts.title: Wongari (Dingo) Rearing and Emergence Season
alerts.description: Limiting dingo-human interactions, particularly during rearing and emergence season, is critical to the welfare of pups. alerts.details:
Limiting dingo-human interactions, particularly during rearing and emergence season, is critical to the welfare of pups. This is a particularly important time for pups to learn natural hunting and survival skills and to avoid habituation towards people. Take particular care and slow down when driving on Kgari - pups are exploring their environment, and this is the time they are most at risk of vehicle strike. Give dingoes space, Kgari is their place.

Dingo rearing and emergence season means:

  • Dingo pups will venture out of their dens and explore their surroundings
  • Adult dingoes will be teaching their young natural hunting and survival skills
  • Dingoes may be determined and assertive in their search for food and females will aggressively defend their young
  • Female dingoes that are feeding young can lose condition and become naturally lean during this time
  • Every time a dingo receives food from people its chance of survival is reduced – let young wongari grow up wild, do not feed them or leave food available

Visitors, tour operators and residents are advised to Be dingo-safe! on K’gari. It is recommended that families with young children camp in fenced QPWS camping areas at Lake Boomanjin, Central Station, Dundubara, Waddy Point and eastern beach fenced areas (Wongai, One Tree Rocks, Cornwells, Eli), or at fenced private camping areas at Dilli Village or Cathedral Beach.

Be dingo-safe! Visit https://parks.detsi.qld.gov.au/parks/kgari-fraser/about/wongari-dingoes/dingo-safe

  • NEVER feed dingoes.
  • Always stay within arm’s reach of children, even small teenagers.
  • Walk in groups and carry a long dingo safety stick.
  • Do not run or jog outside fenced areas - this can attract a dingo’s attention and trigger their instinct to chase.
  • Camp in fenced areas when possible.
  • Secure all rubbish, fish, bait and tackle (even on boats).
  • Never store food, food containers or scented items in tents.
  • No food to lakeshores.

Report dingo encounters – email dingo.ranger@detsi.qld.gov.au, tell the nearest QPWS

ranger, or phone (07) 4127 9150 – mobile phone charges may apply. Take note of location,

vehicle registration, dingo ear tag colour, number and which ear.

For further information about wongari (dingoes) on K’gari (Fraser Island) please visit

https://parks.detsi.qld.gov.au/parks/kgari-fraser/about/wongari-dingoes

alerts.description: Permits for the entire 2027 Thorsborne Trail hiking season will be made available on 15 December 2026 at 10am (Queensland time).
alerts.details:
Permits for the entire 2027 Thorsborne Trail hiking season will be made available on 15 December 2026 at 10am (Queensland time).

The 2027 hiking season is 1 March – 31 December. The standard annual seasonal closure period of 1 January – 28 February will remain in place due to the increased risk of unsafe conditions at this time of year.

12 self-sufficient independent hiking permits are available to start the trail each day. Starting with the 2027 season, the refund policy for the Thorsborne Trail is changing; customers must cancel permits more than 14 days before their start date to get a refund (previously this was 2 days). More information on the new refund policy will be made available in the coming months.

Some key reminders:

  • Your permit start and end dates must match the dates you intend to hike. Penalties may apply for ‘ghost bookings’ where a permit is purchased but not used.
  • Book your vessel transfers as soon as your trail booking is confirmed.
  • If your plans change before your hike, please modify or cancel your permit (see booking page for details). Returning unused spaces back to the booking systems allows other hikers to book them and supports local businesses by utilising the available capacity.

Visit qld.gov.au/ThorsborneTrailHikingSeasons for information and updates about the 2027 season’s permit release. This page contains FAQs and information about how to be best prepared for the permit release.

Visit the Thorsborne Trail booking page to familiarise yourself with the process well before the permit release, as permits for the peak hiking season (May-September) will sell out within an hour of the release. Be prepared with backup dates if you are initially unsuccessful.

alerts.title: Catfish Activity in Designated Swimming Area
alerts.description: Native eel-tailed catfish are currently breeding in this area. During the breeding season, male catfish build large circular nests from gravel and pebbles on the lake bed and actively guard their eggs and young. While normally harmless, catfish may nip swimmers who come too close to a nest as part of their natural defensive behaviour. Visitors are encouraged to avoid disturbing visible nests and take care when swimming or wading in shallow water.

Native eel-tailed catfish are currently breeding in this area. During the breeding season, male catfish build large circular nests from gravel and pebbles on the lake bed and actively guard their eggs and young. While normally harmless, catfish may nip swimmers who come too close to a nest as part of their natural defensive behaviour. Visitors are encouraged to avoid disturbing visible nests and take care when swimming or wading in shallow water.

If bitten or injured by a catfish:

  1. Wash the wound thoroughly with clean water.
  2. Apply an antiseptic to help reduce the risk of infection.
  3. Monitor the injury for signs of infection, including increasing redness, swelling, warmth or discharge.
  4. Seek medical attention if the wound is deep, symptoms worsen, or a fin spine injury causes significant pain or swelling.

alerts.details:
A fire prohibition is active from Monday 12 October 2026 to Friday 15 January 2027 due to the current weather forecast and increased risk of bushfire.

Fires must not be lite anywhere in:

  • Blackbraes National Park
  • White Mountains National Park
  • Porcupine Gorge National Park

During the fire prohibition, only fully enclosed cooking and heating applicances that meet the below requirements are permitted.

The appliance:

•            Must use gas or manufactured fuel (eg. briquettes). Manufactured fuel does not include milled timber or sawn/cut tree parts.

•            Must be used only for cooking and/or heating.

•            Must be a minimum of 20cm off the ground and more than 2m from flammable materials, which includes vegetation.

•            Must not have the potential to generate airborne embers or possibly ignite nearby ground fuels.

•            Must be fully self-contained (heat source enclosed and no exposed flame) and never left unattended when in use. 

Appliances that are not fully self-contained, such as braziers, are not permitted.

All appliances, materials and burnt fuel must be removed from the area on your departure.

Visitors must comply with this fire prohibition, on-site signs and any directions given by Rangers. Penalties apply.

alerts.title: Drive with care during marine turtle nesting season
alerts.description: From November to May, you may see turtles crossing the beach to lay their eggs or hatchlings making their way to the water for the first time. Motorists and visitors to Bribie Island National Park and Recreation Area are asked to minimise disturbance and human impacts to nesting marine turtles.
alerts.details:
From November to May, you may see turtles crossing the beach to lay their eggs or hatchlings making their way to the water for the first time. Motorists and visitors to Bribie Island National Park and Recreation Area are asked to minimise disturbance and human impacts to nesting marine turtles.

When driving on the beach:

  • Plan to travel at 2 hours either side of low tide.
  • Avoid driving on the beach at night. This is when turtles will lay their eggs, and hatchlings are most likely to be emerging. Exercise caution and look out for turtles and turtle hatchlings when traversing the beach. If travelling to Ocean Beach camping area after dark, if possible, use the Northern Access Track.
  • If turtles are making their way across the beach - slow down, stop and wait for the turtles to reach the ocean or the dunes. Penalties apply to visitors disturbing turtle hatchlings or turtle nests.
  • Driving over vegetated dunes is dangerous and prohibited. It is damaging to the environment and can crush turtle nests. Penalties apply.

‘Cut the glow to help turtles go’. Artificial lights can affect a turtle’s ability to see the natural horizon over the ocean. Hatchlings can become disoriented, veer from their natural path and head towards the artificial light. When camping during the nesting season you can help cut the glow of lights affecting beaches by switching off unnecessary lights on the beach after 7.30pm.

To report marine animal strandings (of sick, injured or dead turtles, dolphin, dugongs or whales) download the QWildlife app. or call 1300 130 372.

For your safety please be alert for nearby wildlife.

Please observe all signage, barriers and directions from rangers and do not enter closed areas.

Please monitor park alerts on the department's website for updated information.

alerts.title: Safety advice: Dingoes sighted in area, Baldy-Yabi circuit walk, Herberton Range State Forest and Baldy Mountain Forest Reserve
alerts.description: Dingoes inhabit Herberton Range State Forest and Baldy Mountain Forest Reserve and have the potential to be dangerous to humans. The risk of dangerous behaviour is greatly increased in dingoes that have become habituated to humans through feeding or other encouragement.
alerts.details:
Dingoes inhabit Herberton Range State Forest and Baldy Mountain Forest Reserve and have the potential to be dangerous to humans. The risk of dangerous behaviour is greatly increased in dingoes that have become habituated to humans through feeding or other encouragement.

Always Be dingo-safe!

For your safety:

  • Walk in pairs or groups.
  • Supervise children—keep them within arm’s reach.
  • Always keep your distance. Never approach a dingo.
  • Never run—it can trigger a chase or attack response in dingoes.
  • Never feed or interact with dingoes—dingoes may become aggressive.

While dogs are permitted on a leash on the Baldy-Yabi circuit walk, they may attract the natural curiosity of dingoes. For your safety and that of you dog, ensure they remain on their leash and that you can maintain full control, in case there’s an interaction with a dingo.

Report any incidents of aggressive dingo behaviour to Atherton Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service office – ph: 4091 8100.

Dingoes and all other wildlife are protected here. It is an offence to feed or make food available to a dingo, or to intentionally attract or disturb a dingo. Penalties apply.

alerts.title: Wongari (Dingo) safety reminder
alerts.description: QPWS Rangers on Kgari are urging visitors to be dingo-safe at all times. Limiting dingo-human interactions is critical to the welfare and safety of dingoes and people. It is particularly important that dingoes learn natural hunting and survival skills and that habituation towards people is prevented. Take particular care and slow down when driving to avoid injuring dingoes and other wildlife.
alerts.details:
QPWS Rangers on Kgari are urging visitors to be dingo-safe at all times. Limiting dingo-human interactions is critical to the welfare and safety of dingoes and people. It is particularly important that dingoes learn natural hunting and survival skills and that habituation towards people is prevented. Take particular care and slow down when driving to avoid injuring dingoes and other wildlife.

Give dingoes space, K’gari is their place. Every time a dingo receives food from people its chance of survival is reduced – let wongari grow up wild, do not feed them or leave food available.

Visitors, tour operators and residents are advised to always Be dingo-safe! on K’gari. It is strongly recommended that families with young children camp in fenced QPWS camping areas at Lake Boomanjin, Central Station, Dundubara, Waddy Point and eastern beach fenced areas (Wongai, One Tree Rocks, Cornwells, Eli), or at fenced private camping areas at Dilli Village or Cathedral Beach.

Be dingo-safe! Visit https://parks.detsi.qld.gov.au/parks/kgari-fraser/about/wongari-dingoes/dingo-safe

  • NEVER feed dingoes.
  • Always stay within arm’s reach of children, even small teenagers.
  • Walk in groups and carry a long dingo safety stick.
  • Do not run or jog outside fenced areas - this can attract a dingo’s attention & trigger their instinct to chase.
  • Camp in fenced areas when possible.
  • Secure all rubbish, fish, bait and tackle (even on boats).
  • Never store food, food containers or scented items in tents.
  • No food to lakeshores.

Report dingo encounters – email dingo.ranger@detsi.qld.gov.au, tell the nearest QPWS

ranger, or phone (07) 4127 9150 – mobile phone charges may apply. Take note of location, vehicle registration, dingo ear tag colour, number and which ear.

In an emergency call Triple Zero (000) for immediate assistance.

For further information about wongari (dingoes) on K’gari please visit

https://parks.detsi.qld.gov.au/parks/kgari-fraser/about/wongari-dingoes

Your safety is our concern, but your responsibility.

Please monitor park alerts on the department's website for updated information.

alerts.title: Kgari Great Walk
alerts.description: Due to the Higher-Risk Weather Season typically experienced on Kgari during the warmer months, seasonal restrictions on forward bookings for the Kgari Great Walk are implemented annually from 1 November to 28 February.
alerts.details:
Due to the Higher-Risk Weather Season typically experienced on Kgari during the warmer months, seasonal restrictions on forward bookings for the Kgari Great Walk are implemented annually from 1 November to 28 February.

During this period, the liklihood of bushfires, heatwaves, flooding and tropical cyclones increases. Restricting forward bookings helps minimise the potential impacts on visitors should the walk, or sections of the walk, need to be closed at short notice due to changing weather conditions or other safety concerns.

Following an assessment of current conditions some sections of the K'gari Great Walk have been approved to remain open until 31 December 2026.

The following sections, hiker camps and feeder tracks remain closed under the seasonal closure arrangements:

  • Hook Point to Central Station (southern section)
  • Jabiru hiker's camp
  • Boomanjin hiker's camp
  • Benaroon hiker's camp
  • Markwell's feeder track
  • Wanggoolba feeder track
  • Dundonga feeder track
  • Winnum feeder track

QPWS Rangers will continue to monitor and assess conditions, with sections of the walk and associated camping areas progressively reopened when conditions permit. The next review of the K'gari Great Walk's opening status will be undertaken by 24 December 2026.
